summary.title: The Software Engineer's Guidebook
summary.one_liner: A reference book by Gergely Orosz covering career growth, leveling expectations and day-to-day engineering practice from mid-level developer to staff and principal engineer.
keywords: how to grow as a software engineer
takeaways: The book is organized into six parts, with Parts 1 and 6 applying to all engineering levels and Parts 2 to 5 covering increasingly senior levels.
Topics include career paths, owning your career, performance reviews, promotions, switching jobs, and team structure.
Leveling definitions are aligned closer to Big Tech and scaleups, and expectations can vary between companies.
Intended as a reference to revisit as your career grows: skim familiar chapters and focus on levels you are aiming for.
Available in hardcover, softcover, ebook, audiobook and several translations.
summary.summary: The page is the landing page for The Software Engineer's Guidebook by Gergely Orosz, describing a book on navigating senior, tech lead, staff and principal roles at tech companies and startups. It lays out the table of contents across six parts, from developer career fundamentals through senior engineer, tech lead, and staff/principal engineer topics, plus a conclusion. The page explains the intended use as a reference book and notes that the content targets software engineers, with a smaller applicable portion for other roles. Most of the remaining text is purchasing options, translations and reviews.
